answers.note: Thorough, practical plan with a clear termly timeline, leadership commitments and impact checks, but it asserts that whole-class feedback and quizzes work without citing any evidence.
Concise and workable triage with a review after four weeks, but it gives no evidence for whole-class feedback and only touches on what leaders will look for in book checks.
Grounded in the DfE 2016 marking review, it names specific low-value marking to drop, says in writing what leaders will check, and sets out a measured pilot with clear owners.
Well-timed 20-minute plan that builds on ck, models a pure /sh/, uses only decodable words and includes dictation and a short caption to read.
Solid, engaging session with decodable words, but the sentence reading is only a challenge for quicker children, and it wrongly lists 'a' and 'in' as tricky words.
Clear structure with sentences to read, but it uses 'wish' even though w has not been taught (including in the exit check), and reading cards with each of 26 children runs past 20 minutes.
Accurate, well-interleaved task with a diagram question, evaluation and a full key, but 10 recall questions, a diagram, an extended answer and self-marking are hard to fit into 15 minutes.
Strong mark scheme and good chains of reasoning, but no diagram is required, and a full analytical paragraph with evaluation in about four minutes is unrealistic.
Clearly labelled micro/macro mix with application questions, an AD/AS diagram item, marking points for every question and a realistic 12+3 minute split.
